To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intracytoplasmically synthesized Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ) are decreased in adenoids as compared to peripheral lymphocytes.
the Th1 cytokines, IFN-γ and IL-2, are produced in lower amounts in adenoidal lymphocytes, as compared to peripheral lymphocytes, whereas the Th2 cytokine, IL-4, is produced in similar quantities.
the Th1 cytokines, IFN-γ and IL-2, are differentially expressed in adenoidal and peripheral lymphocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune response to the adenoid, which is an important lymphoid tissue in the upper respiratory tract and the site of the most common bacterial infections.
the development of a multiparameter flow cytometry assay that can be utilized to detect cytokines within the lymphocytes in the human adenoids and peripheral blood.
the study of the immune system in children with recurrent respiratory tract infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adenoidal and circulating peripheral blood CD4 lymphocyte subsets are similar with regard to their cytokine production.
the adenoidal lymphocytes are more Th2 than Th1, whereas the peripheral blood lymphocytes are more balanced between Th2 and Th1.
the adenoid is not just an enlarged lymph node.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Th2 cytokine production is increased and the Th1 cytokine production is decreased in adenoidal lymphocytes as compared to peripheral lymphocytes.
the adenoid is a site of Th1/Th2 imbalance, and the Th1/Th 2 imbalance is more profound in the CD8 lymphocytes than in the CD4 lymphocytes.
the adenoid is a site where the immune system is activated and the Th1 response is down-regulated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flow cytometry is a powerful tool for the analysis of cytokine production at the single-cell levels.
cytokine production in adenoidal lymphocytes is different from cytokine production by peripheral blood lymphocytes.
flow cytometry is a powerful technique to study intracytoplasmatic cytokine synthesis by single lymphocytes in the study of the immune system.
